Two of the targeted flights were heading to the Polish capital, including an SAS Scandinavian Airlines service from Copenhagen and a LOT Polish Airlines flight originating from London Heathrow airport.

A third incident involved a Ryanair flight traveling from Manchester in the northwestern UK to Murcia in southeastern Spain, where airport operator Aena activated emergency protocols. Spain's Civil Guard inspected the aircraft upon a normal landing, allowing authorities to deactivate the emergency plan. Additionally, a Wizz Air flight arriving from Bergamo, Italy, underwent security checks after landing in Sofia, according to a Bulgarian interior ministry spokesperson.

Tuesday's security scares followed a similar incident on Monday involving a Wizz Air flight from London Luton airport to Sofia, which was forced to divert and make an emergency landing in Budapest after receiving a bomb threat. That incident prompted NATO's air defence alert service to issue an alert, according to Hungarian Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi.

In Warsaw, the SAS flight landed normally at Chopin Airport, where authorities temporarily closed one runway to conduct security checks before passengers disembarked. Meanwhile, the LOT flight scheduled for Chopin was diverted to Warsaw Modlin Airport. Modlin airport spokesman Adam Szablowski stated that passengers were evacuated and the Boeing 737 MAX underwent thorough checks. Finding no explosives, authorities reopened Modlin Airport to resume normal operations.

stories.title: اقوام متحدہ میں روایتی ہتھیاروں سے متعلق پاکستانی قرارداد کثرت رائے سے منظور
stories.summary:
اقوام متحدہ کی جنرل اسمبلی کی فرسٹ کمیٹی نے بھاری اکثریت سے روایتی ہتھیاروں کے کنٹرول سے متعلق پاکستان اور بیلاروس کی مشترکہ قرارداد منظور کر لی ہے۔ 193 رکنی باڈی میں اس قرارداد کو 180 ووٹوں کے ساتھ کامیابی ملی، جس کی حمایت نہ صرف امریکہ اور چین بلکہ انڈیا کے روایتی دوست روس نے بھی کی۔ اس قرارداد کی مخالفت کرنے والے ممالک میں صرف انڈیا اور اسرائیل شامل تھے۔

قرارداد کے متن کے مطابق روایتی ہتھیاروں کے کنٹرول کی کوششوں کو بنیادی طور پر علاقائی اور ذیلی علاقائی میکانزم کے ذریعے آگے بڑھایا جانا چاہیے، اور اس کا مقصد فوجی دستوں کی تعداد کو کم سے کم سطح پر رکھ کر علاقائی سلامتی کو مضبوط بنانا ہے۔ پاکستان نے اس منظوری کو اپنی سفارتی کامیابی قرار دیتے ہوئے کہا ہے کہ یہ ہتھیاروں پر قابو پانے کی کوششوں کے لیے عالمی برادری کی وسیع حمایت کا ثبوت ہے۔

دوسری طرف انڈیا نے اس قرارداد کی شدید مخالفت کرتے ہوئے اس کے خلاف ووٹ دیا۔ اقوام متحدہ میں انڈیا کے مستقل مشن کے فرسٹ سیکریٹری انمول شیر بیدی نے مؤقف اختیار کیا کہ سیکیورٹی کے خدشات صرف علاقائی یا ذیلی علاقائی حدود تک محدود نہیں رہ سکتے اور روایتی ہتھیاروں کا کنٹرول ایک عالمی مسئلہ ہے۔ انڈیا نے اس بات پر بھی تشویش ظاہر کی کہ اقوام متحدہ کے اسلحہ کمیشن کو اس موضوع پر دوبارہ کام سونپنے کی ضرورت نہیں ہے کیونکہ اس حوالے سے پہلے ہی 1993، 1999 اور 2017 میں متفقہ رہنما خطوط اور سفارشات طے پا چکی ہیں۔

ماہرین کے مطابق روس کی جانب سے اس قرارداد کی حمایت کو انڈیا کے خلاف کوئی نیا اقدام نہیں بلکہ اس کی دیرینہ پالیسی کا تسلسل قرار دیا جا رہا ہے۔ اس قرارداد میں کسی بھی قسم کی پابند علاقائی ہتھیاروں کی حد مقرر نہیں کی گئی اور نہ ہی یہ کسی ملک کی دفاعی خریداری پر پابندی عائد کرتی ہے، بلکہ اس کا بنیادی مقصد بات چیت کے ذریعے علاقائی معاہدوں اور اعتماد سازی کے اقدامات کو فروغ دینا ہے۔

stories.title: Pakistani Leaders Review Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Emergency and Reforms
stories.summary:
Leaders from the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz and the Pakistan Peoples Party convened a consultative meeting in Islamabad to evaluate the situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa following the implementation of emergency and governor's rule. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif led the discussions, which were also attended by PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari alongside a delegation comprising Senate Chairman Yousuf Raza Gilani, Senator Sherry Rehman, and Raja Pervez Ashraf. Additionally, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti participated in the talks alongside federal cabinet members and senior officials.

During the session, Governor Kundi updated the prime minister regarding administrative steps and ongoing terrorism concerns within Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, while Chief Minister Bugti briefed attendees on the security climate in Balochistan. The participants also addressed the establishment of the proposed Parliamentary Committee on Electoral Reforms. Prime Minister Sharif emphasized that this committee should be formed promptly, prompting Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari to confirm that his party will soon submit its nominees to National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq.

In a separate engagement, Prime Minister Sharif met with Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir. A source at the Prime Minister's Office indicated that this discussion encompassed a comprehensive review of conditions across all provinces. The consultations highlight ongoing administrative coordination between the federal government and key provincial stakeholders amid pressing security challenges.

The high-level meetings underscore the central government's focus on maintaining stability and advancing legislative priorities, such as electoral reforms, during a politically sensitive period. By engaging closely with military leadership and key political allies like the PPP, the administration aims to present a unified approach to governance and regional security across the country.

stories.title: Keisha Lance Bottoms Wins Georgia Governor Race, Making History
stories.summary:
Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms secured a victory in the Georgia gubernatorial race, defeating Republican businessman Rick Jackson according to media projections. With this win, Bottoms becomes the first Black woman elected governor of a United States state, as well as the first female governor in Georgia history. She succeeds outgoing Republican Governor Brian Kemp, who reached his term limit after two consecutive terms. Bottoms, aged 56, previously served as the mayor of Atlanta, as a senior adviser to former President Joe Biden, and as the director of the White House Office of Public Engagement.

The historic outcome represents a major milestone for Black women in American politics, who have historically constituted a core segment of the Democratic base while remaining underrepresented in top executive positions. Concurrently, Stacey Plaskett won election as governor of the United States Virgin Islands on the same evening, achieving the distinction of becoming the first Black woman elected governor of a US jurisdiction. These victories highlight shifting dynamics within American political representation.

Bottoms' success also marks a profound transformation in Georgia politics, where Black voters have driven a multi-generation and multiracial coalition that turned the historically Republican state into a competitive national battleground. Republicans had held the Georgia governor's office for over twenty years prior to this election. Her opponent, Jackson, had campaigned on a platform emphasizing tax cuts, public safety, and reduced government regulation as an outsider candidate.

The election took place amidst midterm contests across the country that will determine control of the United States Congress for the remainder of President Donald Trump's term. Bottoms' breakthrough follows the 2018 and 2022 gubernatorial campaigns of Stacey Abrams, whose organizing efforts laid the groundwork for subsequent Democratic successes in the state, including victories in US Senate races and presidential voting.

stories.title: بی بی سی اردو نے موبائل ایپ متعارف کرا دی
stories.summary:
بی بی سی اردو نے اپنی نئی موبائل ایپ لانچ کر دی ہے، جس کے ذریعے صارفین اب علاقائی اور عالمی خبریں، تفصیلی تجزیے اور معلوماتی مواد براہ راست اپنے موبائل فون یا ٹیبلٹ پر حاصل کر سکتے ہیں۔ یہ تمام مواد بی بی سی ورلڈ سروس کی نئی ایپ کے اندر دستیاب کیا گیا ہے۔

صارفین متعلقہ ایپ سٹور یا گوگل پلے سے اس ایپ کو ڈاؤن لوڈ کر سکتے ہیں اور پھر 'بی بی سی نیوز اردو' کے ایڈیشن کا انتخاب کر کے پاکستان اور دنیا بھر کے مختلف حصوں سے بی بی سی کے صحافیوں کی تیار کردہ رپورٹس دیکھ اور پڑھ سکتے ہیں۔ اس پلیٹ فارم کے ذریعے لائیو کوریج، خبریں اور ویڈیوز ایک ہی جگہ پر دستیاب ہوں گی۔

یاد رہے کہ یہ ایپ برطانیہ اور امریکہ میں دستیاب نہیں ہے اور اس کا کوئی انگریزی زبان کا ایڈیشن موجود نہیں ہے۔ برطانوی نشریاتی ادارہ بی بی سی دنیا بھر میں 45 زبانوں میں مستند خبریں اور معلومات فراہم کرتا ہے اور ہفتہ وار پانچ کروڑ سے زائد افراد تک رسائی رکھتا ہے۔

stories.title: Kusal Mendis Guides Sri Lanka to Recovery in Warm-Up Match
stories.summary:
Kusal Mendis anchored a resilient batting display as the visiting Sri Lankan side reached 162 for five against Patron’s XI during a warm-up fixture at the Islamabad Cricket Club. Having won the toss and elected to bat, Sri Lanka experienced a troubled beginning after losing three quick wickets for just 40 runs. Mendis stepped up to steer the innings, remaining unbeaten on 45 runs from 48 deliveries while hitting eight boundaries to maintain an aggressive momentum despite early setbacks. Anjala Bandara supported him at the crease, finishing not out on seven runs.

Earlier in the match, Lahiru Udara provided a vital foundational knock by scoring 65 runs from 105 balls, which included seven fours and three sixes. Udara's innings proved essential after opening batsman Pasindu Sooriyabandara fell for eight and Dinesh Chandimal was dismissed without scoring, both victims of bowler Saqib Khan. Dhananjaya De Silva chipped in with 14 runs before becoming the sole wicket for Mohammad Salman, leaving the visitors in early trouble. Udara subsequently partnered with Mendis to rebuild the total before Ali Shabbir removed Udara and later dismissed Sonal Dinusha for ten runs.

Among the bowlers, Saqib Khan stood out with figures of 2-25 across 11 overs, while Shoaib Akher Junior delivered an economical performance by conceding just 12 runs in seven overs. Ali Shabbir also claimed two wickets for the hosts. This warm-up encounter serves as crucial preparation for Sri Lanka ahead of their upcoming two-Test series against Pakistan, which commences in Rawalpindi on November 9, followed by the second Test in Lahore on November 17.

stories.title: Democrats Score Key Senate Wins in Midterm Elections
stories.summary:
Democrat Annie Andrews won a United States Senate seat in South Carolina, defeating Darline Graham, the candidate chosen by President Donald Trump, in a state Trump won comfortably two years prior. Andrews, a pediatrician, is the first Democrat to capture a Senate seat in South Carolina in 28 years following a campaign that gained unexpected competitiveness. Alongside Roy Cooper's victory in North Carolina, the results provided Democrats with two of the four additional seats required to secure a Senate majority, though outcomes in several other states remain uncalled.

Additional defensive holds in Georgia and New Hampshire contributed to Democratic momentum, while exit polls and early voting data indicated widespread voter dissatisfaction with national leadership. Approximately half of surveyed voters viewed the midterm elections as a chance to rebuke President Trump, with three-quarters expressing anger or dissatisfaction regarding the country's direction. Key voter concerns centered on affordability, fuel prices, and the consequences of recent foreign policy decisions and import tariffs.

To counter potential political challenges, the US Justice Department deployed one thousand election monitors across all fifty states, marking a historically large monitoring initiative. While federal officials defended the deployment, Democrats criticized the move as potential voter intimidation, pointing out that two-thirds of the targeted jurisdictions had voted for Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election. Local election officials largely reported smooth operations, aside from minor inquiries addressed by state authorities.

Controversies also emerged in other races, including the Alaska Senate contest where allegations surfaced regarding a third-party candidate sharing the name of the incumbent Republican. As vote counting continued across the country, the final balance of power in both the Senate and the House of Representatives remained uncertain. The outcomes carry significant weight for the final two years of President Trump's term, reflecting deep polarization and voter focus on economic pressures.

stories.title: Democrats Gain Early Midterm Victories as Trump Faces Voter Backlash
stories.summary:
Democratic candidates secured several early wins during Tuesday's US midterm elections, capturing a Republican-held Senate seat and advancing into conservative House districts. President Donald Trump faced a challenging electoral judgment amid widespread voter discontent regarding living costs, tariffs, and the US military conflict with Iran, which has driven fuel prices higher. Early results showed Democrats taking a Republican House seat in North Carolina and making gains in Florida.

Notable individual results shifted state-level leadership across the country. Former Atlanta mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms won the Georgia governorship, making history as the nation's first Black woman governor and ending 24 years of Republican rule. In Florida, Trump-backed Byron Donalds became the state's first Black governor, while Republican Ashley Moody retained a Senate seat. Meanwhile, former North Carolina governor Roy Cooper defeated Republican Michael Whatley, claiming a pivotal Senate seat, and Jon Ossoff successfully defended his Senate seat in Georgia. In New Hampshire, Chris Pappas won an open Senate seat to become the first openly gay man in the chamber.

Republicans entered the election holding 53 of the 100 Senate seats, requiring Democrats to achieve a net gain of four to secure control. All 435 House seats were contested, where Democrats needed to flip just three seats to win the chamber. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries noted the country was approaching a dramatic change in direction, which could enable Democrats to block legislative plans, investigate administration policies, and restrict judicial nominees.

Voters frequently cited economic pressures, such as climbing rent, groceries, utility bills, and property taxes, as primary concerns. President Trump defended his record during a final television appearance on Fox News, praising his tariffs, immigration crackdown, and military campaign against Iran. Meanwhile, uncertainty persisted regarding whether Trump would accept unfavorable outcomes, given his history of unsubstantiated claims of election fraud and efforts to overturn his 2020 presidential defeat.

stories.title: Pakistan to Host Four International Squash Events with $439,000 Prizes
stories.summary:
Pakistan is set to host four consecutive international squash tournaments following the conclusion of the ongoing Asian Team Squash Championships in Islamabad. The upcoming competitions will feature top-tier men's and women's players from around the globe, offering a cumulative prize fund of $439,000. This series of events aims to elevate the profile of squash within Pakistan, grant local competitors valuable exposure against international opponents, and reinforce the nation's reputation as a premier sporting venue. While Islamabad will stage the opening tournament, the remaining three events will take place in Karachi.

The action kicks off with the Chief of Air Staff International Squash Championship in Islamabad from November 24 to 28. This $40,000 men's silver-level event will feature Pakistan's Noor Zaman as the top seed, following his recent rise to 25th in the world rankings after winning the World Under-23 Championship. Other seeded Pakistani players include Ashab Irfan at fourth and Mohammad Asim Khan, ranked 68th globally, as the seventh seed, alongside Nasir Iqbal.

Karachi will subsequently stage three tournaments boasting a combined $399,000 in prize money. These include the Chief of Naval Staff Squash Championship from December 1 to 5 at the PN Roshan Khan-Jahangir Khan Squash Complex, which features an $18,000 men's event and a $1,000 women's PSA competition. Afterward, the Creek Club will host the Sindh Open International Squash Championship from December 6 to 10, offering equal prize money for men and women with top international players like Egypt's Youssef Soliman and Salma Hany leading the draws. The series will conclude with the Karachi Open, a Gold-level championship running from January 5 to 10, 2027, featuring a total prize purse of $250,000 distributed evenly between men and women.

stories.title: US Media Projects Democratic Majority Control of the House
stories.summary:
United States media outlets projected on Tuesday that the Democratic Party is on track to secure majority control of the House of Representatives. This projected legislative outcome positions Democrats to challenge the political agenda of President Donald Trump in the upcoming year.

The forecasts emerged as part of the ongoing midterm election coverage, where control of Congress hung in the balance. Winning the House provides the opposition party with significant oversight capabilities.

With a projected majority in the lower chamber, Democrats would be positioned to heavily influence legislative proceedings. They could potentially block administration priorities and launch congressional investigations into federal policies.

The media projections underscore the shifting political dynamics midway through President Trump's second term. The results reflect broader voter discontent that manifested across various congressional contests nationwide.

stories.title: Rethinking Administrative Boundaries and Federal Restructuring Through Public Interest
stories.summary:
Recent political commentary in Pakistan has brought renewed attention to the creation of new provinces, a topic that requires rigorous, inclusive deliberation rather than hasty political sound bites. Restructuring a federation involves deep implications for fiscal imperatives, political representation, public service delivery, and the everyday lives of citizens. Global examples demonstrate that successful administrative changes are rooted in specific legal, political, and economic contexts, addressing clearly defined problems rather than relying solely on political ambition.

International precedents highlight diverse approaches. India established Telangana following extensive public engagement, while Brazil divided Goiás to form Tocantins through constitutionally mandated plebiscitary mechanisms. Russia prioritized consolidation and improved living standards for the Zabaykalsky Krai region, and Timor-Leste established Oé-Cusse to accelerate socioeconomic development. These examples show that redrawing maps must not be treated as a reductive exercise. Instead, administrative changes should represent fundamental state reforms aimed at reducing inequality, democratizing opportunities, and improving public services based on defined public interest.

Specific insights for Pakistan emphasize the need to integrate the empowerment of local governments into the debate on new provinces. Authorities must avoid relying on administrative fiat, illegal referendums, or ethno-linguistic nationalism. Past mistakes, such as leaving local governance structures to provincial discretion under Article 140-A of the 18th Amendment, must not be repeated.

A structured three-step roadmap is proposed to move forward responsibly. First, an independent 'Commission for Citizen-Centric Change' should be established to lead public engagement and technical analysis. Second, a three-dimensional 'Public Interest Test' framework must assess public benefits, fiscal viability, and institutional readiness. Third, these arrangements should be tested in a policy lab setting, with Punjab serving as the primary case review given its size and ongoing debates regarding a south Punjab province, before any nationwide scaling.

stories.title: Trump Faces Critical Midterm Test Amid Low Approval Ratings
stories.summary:
As polls opened across the United States on Tuesday, President Donald Trump faced a significant test of his political standing as Democrats aimed to leverage public dissatisfaction to gain control of Congress. Voters decided all 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 Senate seats, and governorships in 36 states. Although Trump was not personally on the ballot, he urged voters to treat the midterms as a personal referendum. However, national averages from NBC News indicated his approval rating stood at 38 percent against a 60 percent disapproval rate, suggesting his presence could be a liability for Republican candidates.

Foreign policy and local economic pressures complicated Republican campaigns. In Wisconsin, Representative Derrick Van Orden pointed to the US-Israeli war on Iran as a factor dampening Republican voter enthusiasm. In Michigan, Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed focused his campaign on the cost of living and the influence of money in politics. El-Sayed faced severe criticism after Trump characterized him as a security threat and questioned his loyalty, though the candidate rejected the attacks as distractions from core economic problems and maintained a slim lead.

Democrats pursued a net gain of four seats to capture the Senate, though the chamber presented a difficult challenge due to continued Republican support in key states. Winning the House of Representatives appeared more plausible for Democrats, requiring a net gain of just three seats, although success depended heavily on turnout in competitive districts that Trump previously won in 2024.

Amid persistent concerns regarding voting integrity, the US Justice Department deployed approximately 1,000 election monitors and observers across all 50 states for the first time in history. Coordinated by the Civil Rights Division, the initiative aimed to ensure compliance with federal voting rights laws, protect against intimidation and discrimination, and safeguard voters with disabilities against the backdrop of Trump's unverified claims of election fraud.

stories.title: Democrat Annie Andrews Wins US Senate Seat in South Carolina Upset
stories.summary:
Democrat pediatrician Annie Andrews secured a victory in a US Senate race in conservative South Carolina on Tuesday, defeating Republican Darline Graham. This outcome marks the first time a Democrat has won a Senate seat in the state in 28 years, serving as a notable gain for the Democratic Party as they attempt to overturn the 53-47 Republican majority in the Senate. The contest took place in a state previously considered safe for Republicans, highlighting a broader public rejection of President Donald Trump and his economic management during his first two years in office, alongside voter frustration regarding high living costs, diesel prices, and the conflict involving Iran.

The vacancy arose following the death of longtime Republican US Senator Lindsey Graham. Following his passing, President Trump endorsed Senator Graham's sister, Darline Graham, to compete for a full six-year term, despite her limited political background and low public profile. Although she secured the Republican nomination through a special runoff election with presidential support, she admitted during the primary campaign that she lacked extensive knowledge of national security issues. President Trump also visited the state for a campaign rally as the contest tightened, during which Darline Graham described her opponent as "batshit crazy," prompting Andrews to question whether wanting affordable groceries and gas constituted insanity.

Financial investments in the race were substantial, with Andrews outraising her Republican opponent by $22 million. Outside Republican organizations spent $27 million to defend the seat, whereas Democratic groups allocated $24 million toward flipping it. President Trump carried the same state by an 18-percentage-point margin only two years prior, but his approval ratings experienced historic lows ahead of this midterm election contest, enabling competitive dynamics in a traditionally uncompetitive region.

stories.title: Keisha Lance Bottoms Makes History as First Black Woman Governor of Georgia
stories.summary:
Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms secured a victory in the Georgia gubernatorial race on Tuesday, making history as the first Black woman and the first female governor elected in the state. Bottoms, who is 56 years old, defeated Republican businessman and healthcare staffing company founder Rick Jackson. She will succeed outgoing Republican Governor Brian Kemp, who is concluding his tenure after serving two consecutive terms. Previously, Bottoms served as the mayor of Atlanta and worked as a senior adviser to former President Joe Biden, in addition to directing the White House Office of Public Engagement.

This outcome represents a significant milestone for Black women in American politics, who have historically formed a vital foundation for the Democratic Party while remaining severely underrepresented in top elected positions nationwide. On the same evening, Stacey Plaskett achieved a similar milestone by winning election as governor of the US Virgin Islands, becoming the first Black woman to lead a US territory. Bottoms' triumph also reflects a profound political transformation in Georgia, where Black voters built the core coalition that converted a dependably Republican state into a competitive national battleground after more than two decades of continuous Republican governance.

The campaign highlighted starkly different political approaches, with Jackson positioning himself as an outsider centered on public safety, regulatory reduction, and tax cuts. Bottoms' success arrives eight years after fellow Democrat Stacey Abrams became the inaugural Black woman nominated for governor by a major political organization. Although Abrams was unsuccessful in her 2018 and 2022 gubernatorial bids, her organizational efforts successfully cultivated a diverse, multiracial coalition that elevated voter participation, facilitated the election of two Democratic US senators, and secured the state's electoral votes for a Democratic presidential contender for the first time in decades.

stories.title: Fire at Panasonic Factory in Taiwan Leaves Five Injured and Two Missing
stories.summary:
A fire erupted on Wednesday at a manufacturing facility located in Taiwan operated by a subsidiary of Japan's Panasonic, according to local authorities in Hsinchu County. The incident resulted in injuries to five individuals who were promptly transported to a hospital for medical care, while two other people remained unaccounted for following the blaze. Panasonic did not immediately issue a statement in response to inquiries regarding the emergency.

The affected facility, operated by Panasonic Industrial Devices Materials Taiwan, plays a critical role in the region's technology supply chain. The unit manufactures essential materials utilized in printed circuit boards, which are foundational components required for the production of various electronic devices, including computers and advanced artificial intelligence servers.

stories.title: Depleted Bayern Munich Defeats Atletico Madrid in the Champions League
stories.summary:
A severely depleted Bayern Munich squad secured a dominant 2-0 victory away against Atletico Madrid in a Tuesday Champions League fixture. Teenage German forward Lennart Karl opened the scoring by capitalizing on a defensive error, while Konrad Laimer added a second goal to seal the win in Madrid. Bayern arrived with a significant injury list that included Jamal Musiala, Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry, and Ismael Saibari, alongside head coach Vincent Kompany, who was sidelined with a meningitis-related illness. Despite these absences, recent Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane and captain Joshua Kimmich guided the team to a comprehensive triumph.

The breakthrough arrived when Atletico defender Robin Le Normand held onto the ball too long, allowing Karl to pick his pocket and loft a shot over goalkeeper Jan Oblak. In the second half, Bayern doubled their lead when Kane delivered a precise pass into the path of Laimer, who struck a powerful shot in off the crossbar. Although Kane did not score—thereby missing the opportunity to equal Cristiano Ronaldo's record of scoring in 11 consecutive Champions League games—he provided a key assist and commanded the attacking line effectively alongside Michael Olise and Karl.

Atletico Madrid struggled to find a response as Diego Simeone made tactical changes, but Bayern's defense easily neutralized the hosts in the closing stages. Dayot Upamecano even had a header disallowed late in the match for an offensive foul. With this result, Bayern climbed to eighth place on the 36-team table with two wins and two draws, while Atletico dropped to 22nd place following the conclusion of Tuesday's matches.

stories.title: کراچی: سندھ ہائیکورٹ نے کمسن بچی کے قتل کے ملزم کی سزائے موت عمر قید میں بدل دی
stories.summary:
سندھ ہائیکورٹ نے کراچی میں کمسن بچی کو زیادتی کے بعد قتل کرنے کے کیس کا فیصلہ سناتے ہوئے ملزم عرفان کی سزائے موت کو عمر قید میں تبدیل کر دیا۔ عدالت میں یہ فیصلہ ملزم کی جانب سے دائر کردہ اپیل پر سماعت کے بعد دیا گیا۔

عدالت میں سماعت کے دوران ملزم کے وکیل لیاقت گبول ایڈووکیٹ نے مؤقف اختیار کیا کہ ٹرائل کورٹ کی جانب سے سنائی گئی سزا میں قانونی تقاضے پورے نہیں کیے گئے تھے اور گواہان کے بیانات میں بھی تضاد پایا جاتا تھا۔

پراسیکیوشن کے مطابق ملزم عرفان نے 8 دسمبر 2022 کو مبینہ ٹاؤن تھانے کی حدود میں ایک گھر میں گھس کر پلمبر کا کام کرنے کے دوران بچی کو اکیلا پا کر زیادتی کا نشانہ بنایا اور بعد میں اس کا گلا دبا کر قتل کر دیا۔ اس واقعے کا مقدمہ مقتولہ بچی کے والد کی مدعیت میں درج کیا گیا تھا۔

جون 2026 میں ایڈیشنل ڈسٹرکٹ اینڈ سیشن جج شرقی نے اس ملزم کو جرم ثابت ہونے پر سزائے موت کا حکم سنایا تھا جسے اب سندھ ہائیکورٹ نے عمر قید کی سزا میں تبدیل کر دیا ہے۔

stories.title: Indian Rupee Recovers on Strong Equity Inflows and Weakening US Dollar
stories.summary:
The Indian rupee was positioned for a slight recovery on Wednesday, aided by renewed capital inflows into domestic equities and a weakening US dollar driven by midterm election outcomes pointing toward potential Democratic dominance in Washington. Currency traders projected the rupee to open near 94.70, following a previous close of 94.74 on Tuesday. Meanwhile, the dollar index experienced a 0.3% decline, while US Treasury yields and equity futures dropped as financial markets priced in expectations of a Democratic majority in both the House and the Senate.

Analysts at ING Bank noted that while midterm results typically do not cause structural transformations in foreign exchange markets, a dual Democratic congressional victory could generate short-term downward pressure on the dollar. They added that stricter regulatory prospects under such a government could impact artificial intelligence stocks, a trend that recently influenced broader currency movements. While Asian currencies demonstrated muted reactions and regional markets followed the downward trajectory of US futures, Indian equities attracted significant foreign capital as investors rotated away from slowing technology-driven trades.

Indian stocks have experienced a 5% rally across four sessions, supported by expectations that the country may modify or eliminate long-term capital gains taxes for international investors. Foreign institutional investors injected over $700 million into Indian equities on Tuesday alone, elevating total purchases over a three-day span to approximately $1.5 billion and offering a local hedge amid global tech sector pullbacks.

stories.title: Pakistan Government Seeks Opposition Representation on Electoral Reforms Panel
stories.summary:
The government of Pakistan has officially reached out to the opposition to request names for the newly proposed Parliamentary Committee on Electoral Reforms, aimed at ensuring a transparent and fair electoral process. Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry contacted PTI chief whip in the National Assembly Aamir Dogar to ask for opposition nominations. However, the opposition has dismissed the committee as a futile exercise due to ongoing grievances.

Mr Dogar highlighted several major concerns preventing participation, including the recent imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the detention of the provincial chief minister, and the arrest of numerous PTI leaders. He also reiterated claims that the PTI's mandate was stolen during the previous general elections and demanded equal representation for the government and the opposition on the panel.

Under the proposed allocation formula presented by Minister Chaudhry, seats are assigned based on National Assembly strength, allocating one seat for every 16 members. The formula grants the PML-N nine seats, the PPP five, and the MQM-P one, with smaller allies receiving seats from the PML-N quota. Meanwhile, the ruling coalition ally PPP has criticized the opposition for delaying the appointment of a new chief election commissioner (CEC), noting that the opposition leader has not met the prime minister for mandatory consultations.

This committee initiative, introduced by National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq, is intended by the government to open doors for broader national consultations, including resolving the long-delayed CEC appointment. While PTI interim Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan indicated the opposition might engage if dialogue is sincere, key opposition figures maintain that current political conditions make cooperation difficult.

stories.title: US Dollar Weakens Ahead of Midterm Election Results and Early Wins
stories.summary:
The US dollar lost ground against major global currencies on Wednesday as markets closely watched early results from the United States midterm elections. The greenback slipped as investors anticipated a strong performance by the Democratic Party, which could potentially result in a congressional sweep and impact future government spending and monetary policies.

In early trading, the euro increased by 0.2% to reach $1.1212, while the Japanese yen strengthened to 158.30 per US dollar. The dollar index, which tracks the currency against a basket of six major peers, decreased by 0.2% to 101.7. Additionally, the yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note dropped by 4 basis points to settle at 4.919%.

According to currency strategist Carol Kong from the Commonwealth Bank of Australia, a Democratic takeover of both the House and the Senate is favored by markets and could drive the dollar down further by restricting government spending. Investors are also monitoring geopolitical risks, including potential post-election escalations in the Middle East that could impact oil prices and subsequently support the US currency.

Other currencies also saw movement amid the broader market backdrop. Sterling climbed to $1.3440 ahead of an anticipated interest rate decision by the Bank of England, while China’s offshore yuan stabilized at 6.6673 per dollar following previous actions by the People’s Bank of China to manage its valuation.

stories.title: US Stock Futures and Dollar Slide on Early Democratic Midterm Wins
stories.summary:
United States stock futures dropped, Treasury yields rallied, and the dollar softened on Wednesday following early Democratic victories in the midterm elections. Investors responded to signs that Democrats might capture control of Congress from President Donald Trump’s Republican Party, introducing uncertainty into future fiscal policies, defense spending, and regulatory frameworks.

Notable early results included former Governor Roy Cooper flipping a Republican Senate seat in North Carolina by defeating Trump-backed candidate Michael Whatley, alongside Democrat Jon Ossoff winning re-election in Georgia. These results bring Democrats closer to securing the net gains needed for a legislative majority, keeping market participants on edge as state-by-state races continue.

Financial markets reacted swiftly to the political shift. S&P 500 futures fell 0.8%, and Nasdaq futures slumped 1.8% amid concerns that a Democratic-led Congress could increase scrutiny on artificial intelligence and big technology companies. Meanwhile, the benchmark US 10-year Treasury yield declined by 6 basis points to 4.906%, and the dollar index dropped 0.32% to 101.39 as the euro and sterling both strengthened.

Across Asia, regional markets retreated as investors balanced these domestic US political developments with corporate earnings and ongoing commodity market trends. The MSCI broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan slipped 0.5%, South Korea’s KOSPI fell 1.6%, and Japan’s Nikkei dropped 3% following a market holiday.

stories.title: کالعدم تنظیم بی ایل اے کے سربراہ بشیر زیب کو عہدے سے ہٹا دیا گیا
stories.summary:
کالعدم علیحدگی پسند تنظیم بلوچ لبریشن آرمی (بی ایل اے) نے ایک پریس ریلیز کے ذریعے اعلان کیا ہے کہ بشیر زیب بلوچ اب تنظیم کے سربراہ کے طور پر کام نہیں کریں گے۔ تنظیم کی سینئر کمانڈ کونسل کے فیصلے کے تحت انہیں ہٹایا گیا ہے اور نئے سربراہ کے نام کا اعلان جلد کیے جانے کا کہا گیا ہے۔ بشیر زیب پچھلے چند برسوں سے پاکستان میں دہشت گردی کے سنگین الزامات کے تحت مطلوب چلے آرہے ہیں۔

نوشکی کے احمدوال سے تعلق رکھنے والے بشیر زیب نے اپنی جوانی کے ایام میں کوئٹہ میں طلبہ سیاست میں نمایاں کردار ادا کیا تھا۔ وہ 2006 سے 2012 تک بلوچ سٹوڈنٹس آرگنائزیشن (بی ایس او آزاد) کے چیئرمین رہے، جو بعد میں حکومتِ پاکستان کی جانب سے ریاست مخالف سرگرمیوں اور شدت پسندوں کو بھرنے کا ذریعہ قرار دیے جانے کے بعد کالعدم قرار دے دی گئی۔ بشیر زیب نے اپنی تحریروں میں ڈاکٹر اللہ نذر اور عسکری نظریات سے متاثر ہو کر بندوق اٹھانے کا ذکر کیا تھا، جس کے بعد وہ بی ایل اے میں شامل ہو گئے تھے۔

سنہ 2017 کے دوران تنظیمی اصولوں کی خلاف ورزی پر بشیر زیب اور اسلم بلوچ کو بی ایل اے سے عارضی طور پر نکالا گیا تھا، جس کے بعد انہوں نے ایک الگ گروہ بنایا۔ تاہم 2018 میں اسلم بلوچ کی ہلاکت کے بعد بی ایل اے کی قیادت بشیر زیب کے ہاتھوں میں آگئی تھی۔ ان کی سربراہی کے دوران تنظیم اور اس کے ذیلی مجید بریگیڈ کے حملوں میں شدت دیکھی گئی، جن میں کراچی میں چینی قونصل خانے پر حملہ، کراچی اسٹاک ایکسچینج، کراچی یونیورسٹی میں خودکش حملہ اور چینی انجینئرز کے قافلے پر حملے جیسے بڑے واقعات شامل ہیں۔

سابقہ حکام کے مطابق بشیر زیب جیسے تعلیم یافتہ فرد کا عسکریت پسند تنظیم کی قیادت تک پہنچنا اس بات کی عکاسی کرتا ہے کہ کس طرح بعض نوجوان ریاست مخالف نظریات کی طرف راغب ہوئے۔ اب جب کہ انہیں سربراہ کے منصب سے ہٹا دیا گیا ہے، سیکیورٹی اور سیاسی حلقوں میں اس تبدیلی کے بی ایل اے کی آئندہ کارروائیوں پر پڑنے والے اثرات کا جائزہ لیا جا رہا ہے۔

stories.title: Gold Prices Rise as Softer Oil Markets Ease Inflationary Pressures
stories.summary:
Gold prices experienced a modest increase during early Asian trading on Wednesday, supported by softer oil prices that helped alleviate broader inflation concerns. Investors are closely monitoring upcoming US midterm election results and crucial labor market data to gauge future monetary policy directions from the Federal Reserve.

Spot gold rose 0.2% to $3,934.75 per ounce, while US gold futures for December delivery increased by 0.1% to $3,943.20. The upward movement in gold was partly driven by a roughly 1% decline in oil prices on Tuesday, which hit four-week lows as markets assessed ongoing diplomatic talks to resolve conflicts in Ukraine and Iran alongside lingering supply disruption fears.

Lower oil prices have reduced near-term inflation expectations, leading traders to reconsider whether the Federal Reserve will maintain high interest rates for an extended period. Currently, CME’s FedWatch tool indicates a 78% probability that the Fed will implement an interest rate increase in December, enhancing the attractiveness of non-yielding assets like gold.

In related precious metals and market forecasts, the World Gold Council announced that India's gold demand is projected to drop to a six-year low in 2026 due to high prices impacting jewelry sales. Among other metals, spot silver dipped 0.2% to $49.67 per ounce, platinum gained 0.3% to $1,422.15, and palladium advanced 0.5% to $938.49.

stories.title: Pakistan Government Introduces New LPG Policy as Power Costs Rise
stories.summary:
The federal government has directed four state-owned enterprises to re-enter the liquefied petroleum gas import business to tackle severe supply shortages and high market prices. Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced the approved policy during a news conference in Islamabad, noting that private importers can also arrange alternative supplies. The state firms involved are Pakistan State Oil, Pakistan LNG Ltd, Sui Southern Gas-LPG, and Parco-LPG. Prime Minister directives will provide subsidised LPG at Rs300-350 per kg for consumers eligible under the Benazir Income Support Programme, financed through a new fund.

Market prices had surged due to disruptions on western borders, causing unauthorised elements to sell gas between Rs700 and Rs800 per kg, well above the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority notified limit of Rs295 per kg for November. Under the new guidelines, state-owned entities will import gas in bulk and publish base prices linked to the Saudi Aramco Contract Price, while local producers will auction lots through a competitive process. Regulatory bodies like the Competition Commission and Ogra will monitor collusive practices and quality standards.

Simultaneously, the power division presented projections at a public hearing before the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority regarding electricity purchase costs for calendar year 2027. Officials from the Central Power Purchasing Agency and Power Planning and Monitoring Company outlined various scenarios, with all base projections exceeding this year's rate of Rs25.32 per unit. The base-case scenario estimated a power purchase price of Rs27.31 per unit, while worst-case projections reached up to Rs29.26 per unit. Industrial consumers criticized the creation of additional entities and high staff salaries for driving up tariffs, while Nepra reserved its decision.

stories.title: Democrats Gain Ground in US Midterm Elections With North Carolina Flip
stories.summary:
Democrats displayed unexpected strength in midterm elections by flipping a Republican-held Senate seat in North Carolina and performing well in several House districts. Former Governor Roy Cooper defeated Trump-backed Republican Michael Whatley in North Carolina, while other contests remained uncounted across the United States. Control of Congress hung in the balance as voters delivered a referendum on the first two years of President Donald Trump's second term.

Exit polls indicated that half of the voters nationwide viewed the midterms as a rebuke of the president, with three-quarters expressing dissatisfaction with the nation's direction. Voter concerns centered around affordability, high fuel prices, and foreign policy issues, including the conflict with Iran. Republicans have historically faced losses during midterm elections, and Trump's approval ratings remained low. The Justice Department deployed 1,000 election monitors across all 50 states, drawing criticism from Democrats who labeled the initiative as potential voter intimidation.

In Alaska, a controversy emerged in the Senate race involving Democratic candidate Mary Peltola after a report noted the appearance of an independent candidate sharing the name of her Republican opponent, Dan Sullivan. The Justice Department initiated a criminal probe and filed a lawsuit to block certification of the election results, although a judge dismissed the lawsuit. With 47 competitive House races closely watched, Democrats aimed to secure the necessary majorities in both the House and the Senate amidst high voter turnout.

stories.title: Spanish Ambassador Calls for Direct Flights and Enhanced Bilateral Trade
stories.summary:
Spanish Ambassador to Pakistan Carlos Aragon emphasized the necessity of initiating direct flights between Pakistan and Spain to significantly boost bilateral trade. Speaking to the business community at the Faisalabad Chamber of Commerce & Industry, he stated that visa processing for business people would be streamlined as a top priority without unnecessary delays. He also highlighted areas of mutual collaboration, such as women empowerment, climate change mitigation, and the promotion of a circular economy.

Aragon noted that Spain's national circular economy strategy includes Spanish companies exporting textile recycling machinery to Pakistan. He pointed out that Spanish universities offer educational opportunities for Pakistani students, whose alumni can help enhance bilateral ties and global soft images. Additionally, he expressed readiness to assist Pakistan's renewable energy sector. Arif Ehsan Malik, President of the FCCI, welcomed the ambassador, highlighting Faisalabad's status as Pakistan's textile engine and inviting Spanish investors to the M3 Industrial Estate.

Malik also proposed collaborations between Spanish design schools and the textile university of Faisalabad to foster innovation in industrial design and fashion. He thanked Spain for granting GSP plus status to Pakistan and mentioned local exporters' compliance with labor and environmental laws. The session concluded with a question-and-answer exchange, followed by the presentation of an FCCI shield to Ambassador Aragon.

stories.title: Trump Admits Iran War Impacted Midterms As Democrats Take Congress
stories.summary:
US President Donald Trump acknowledged that ongoing military conflicts overseas influenced the outcome of Tuesday's midterm elections, which resulted in Democrats capturing majorities in both the US House and Senate. During an interview with Fox News following his return from campaign rallies in Iowa and Kansas, Trump noted that the conflict in Iran weighed heavily on Republican candidates. However, he maintained that voters still supported his management of the situation, stating that people understood the significance of his actions regarding Tehran.

The sweeping legislative setback leaves Trump as a lame duck president for the final two years of his second term, with opposition lawmakers poised to challenge his policy agenda. Addressing potential standoffs, Trump told Fox News that he plans to veto legislation he deems insane, expressing confidence that after a few months of vetoes, both parties would be forced to work together. Meanwhile, a White House official criticized the performance and quality of several Republican contenders on the ballot, arguing that the president did a better job promoting them than they did themselves.

The electoral fallout also claimed prominent party figures, including Texas Governor Greg Abbott, who was unseated by Democrat Gina Hinojosa. Trump blamed Abbott's defeat on him becoming a Republican In Name Only, while the White House signaled that the administration would not quietly accept the legislative shift. Officials hinted at future political retribution against adversaries and raised the prospect of renewed military action against Tehran to address public concerns over fuel prices.

As the results rolled in, top cabinet members and White House staff watched the developments from a reception in the East Room, dining on takeout from The Cheesecake Factory. With the opposition now in full control of Congress, the administration's statement struck a defiant tone regarding future political battles, warning that the president's determination to counter the left wing would only intensify in the wake of the defeat.

stories.title: Federal Minister Salik Defies Defamation Claim Over Corruption Allegations
stories.summary:
Federal Minister for Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development Chaudhry Salik Hussain refused to retract corruption allegations made against the Punjab administration, defying a Rs 5 billion defamation claim filed by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz. Speaking to reporters in Islamabad, the minister maintained that corruption was occurring in the province and stated he had no reason to withdraw his statements. The legal and political confrontation highlighted growing tensions between political figures.

Addressing separate criticisms regarding administrative appointments, Hussain clarified that he did not seek the placement of a deputy commissioner, noting that the officer was already posted when the issue arose. He emphasized the importance of humility for individuals holding authority, praying against pride and arrogance. Reaffirming his stance, the federal minister asserted that his remarks were delivered honestly and should not be interpreted through provincial boundaries or affiliations.

stories.title: Indian Shares Expected to Open Lower Ahead of US Midterms
stories.summary:
Indian shares are projected to open lower on Wednesday, interrupting a four-day winning streak as investors focus on the US midterm election results. The outcome in the United States could impact the Middle East conflict, energy prices, AI data center expansion, and the US fiscal outlook. These factors are closely followed by domestic investors due to higher energy prices and limited local exposure to AI stocks.

GIFT Nifty futures stood at 23,711 at 7:51 a.m. IST, pointing to a weaker opening for the benchmark Nifty 50, which finished at 23,810.85 on Tuesday. Prior to this, the Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex climbed roughly 5% over four sessions, reaching two-month highs driven by strong corporate earnings, decreasing oil prices, and early foreign inflows.

Foreign investors net bought 68.37 billion rupees ($721.66 million) of Indian shares on Tuesday, marking net purchases in five of the last six sessions. Meanwhile, Brent crude futures traded near $103 per barrel after reaching a four-week low amid discussions to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran.

Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, noted that potential easing in foreign outflows, lower energy prices, and optimism regarding tax policy developments could support domestic sentiment. Across Asia, markets dropped 0.7% and US stock futures declined as markets watched whether Democrats could take control of Congress from Republicans.

stories.title: امریکہ کے وسط مدتی انتخابات اور صدر ٹرمپ کے سیاسی مستقبل کا فیصلہ
stories.summary:
امریکہ کے وسط مدتی انتخابات ملک کے سیاسی منظرنامے اور صدر ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ کی صدارت کے بقیہ دو برسوں کے لیے فیصلہ کن حیثیت رکھتے ہیں۔ ان انتخابات میں ووٹرز کانگریس کے دونوں ایوانوں یعنی ایوانِ نمائندگان اور سینیٹ کے ارکان کا انتخاب کر رہے ہیں۔ فی الحال کانگریس کے دونوں ایوانوں پر صدر ٹرمپ کی جماعت ریپبلکن پارٹی کا کنٹرول ہے، لیکن کم ہوتی عوامی مقبولیت اور مہنگائی جیسے مسائل کی وجہ سے ڈیموکریٹس ان انتخابات میں کامیابی کے لیے پرامید ہیں۔

صدر ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ کی عوامی مقبولیت ان کے حلف اٹھانے کے بعد سے مسلسل گراوٹ کا شکار ہے، جو ابتدائی دنوں میں پچاس فیصد سے زائد تھی لیکن رواں برس ایران کے خلاف فضائی حملوں اور اس کے نتیجے میں تیل کی قیمتوں میں اضافے کے بعد گر کر اٹھتی چالیس فیصد کے لگ بھگ یا اس سے بھی نیچے آ چکی ہے۔ تاریخ کے اعداد و شمار گواہ ہیں کہ وسط مدتی انتخابات میں عموماً برسرِ اقتدار صدر کی جماعت کو نشستوں کا نقصان اٹھانا پڑتا ہے، جہاں 1934 کے بعد سے حکمران جماعت کو اوسطاً 27 نشستیں گنوانی پڑی ہیں۔

ایوانِ نمائندگان میں ریپبلکنز کو انتہائی معمولی اکثریت حاصل ہے اور اس کی تمام 435 نشستوں پر فیصلہ کن معرکہ متوقع ہے، جبکہ سینیٹ کی 35 نشستوں پر بھی انتخابات ہو رہے ہیں جہاں ریپبلکنز کو برتری حاصل ہے۔ ڈیموکریٹس کو سینیٹ کا کنٹرول سنبھالنے کے لیے چند غیر یقینی نشستوں پر کامیابی حاصل کرنا لازمی ہوگی۔ اس کے علاوہ معاشی محاذ پر بڑھتی ہوئی مہنگائی، پیٹرول کی بلند قیمتیں اور صحت عامہ کے مسائل ووٹرز کے لیے سب سے اہم موضوعات بنے ہوئے ہیں، جنہیں ڈیموکریٹک امیدوار اپنی مہم کا حصہ بنا رہے ہیں۔

اگرچہ رائے عامہ کے جائزوں میں ڈیموکریٹس کی پوزیشن بہتر بتائی جا رہی ہے، لیکن ریپبلکن پارٹی کو فنڈز کے معاملے میں واضح مالی برتری حاصل ہے جو انتخابی مہم میں اہم کردار ادا کر سکتی ہے۔ اکتوبر کے وسط تک ریپبلکنز اور ان سے جڑے گروہوں کے پاس کروڑوں ڈالر کے فنڈز موجود تھے، جنہیں وہ اشتہارات اور ووٹرز کو متحرک کرنے کے لیے استعمال کر رہے ہیں۔

stories.title: Pakistan Cricket Board Names Shaheens Squad for Asia Cup
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Cricket Board has revealed the 15-member Pakistan Shaheens squad for the upcoming 50-over edition of the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026. The tournament is scheduled to take place in Qatar from November 19 to 29. Defending champions Pakistan Shaheens are placed in Group B alongside India A, Nepal, and the United Arab Emirates. Abdul Samad has been appointed as the captain of the squad to lead the team through their campaign.

Opening their schedule, the Shaheens will play against the UAE on November 20 at the University of Doha Ground, which is the only day fixture for the team. Their remaining group matches are day-night encounters at the West End Park International Stadium, facing India A on November 22 and Nepal on November 24. The semi-finals are slated for November 26 and 27, with the championship final scheduled for Sunday, November 29. Group A consists of Afghanistan A, Bangladesh A, Hong Kong China, and Sri Lanka A.

The squad features a robust batting core alongside captain Abdul Samad, including Hasan Nawaz, Maaz Sadaqat, Haider Ali, Shahzaib Khan, Farhan Yousuf, and Shamyl Hussain, with Rohail Nazir designated as the wicket-keeper. Spin duties will be managed by Danish Aziz, Saad Masood, and Sufyan Moqim. The pace attack is headed by Mohammad Hasnain, supported by Ahmed Daniyal, Akif Javed, and Muhammad Imran Randhawa.

Pakistan holds a strong history in the tournament, having won the last 50-over edition in 2023 in Sri Lanka by defeating India A by 128 runs. They also clinched the previous T20 edition title by edging Bangladesh A in a super-over thriller. Furthermore, Pakistan finished as runners-up in the opening two editions in 2013 and 2017, and secured victory in 2019.

stories.title: Argentine Ambassador Offers Agricultural Expertise to Pakistan
stories.summary:
The Ambassador of the Argentine Republic to Pakistan, Sebastián Sayús, visited the Karachi Chamber of Commerce & Industry to propose Argentina's expertise in advanced agricultural machinery, grain-storage technologies, and post-harvest management. During his address, Ambassador Sayús pointed out that Pakistan suffers annual losses of 10 to 20 percent in grain production and 35 to 40 percent in horticultural produce due to inadequate storage and post-harvest handling. He suggested that modern Argentine storage solutions, such as silo bags and metallic silos, could significantly help Pakistan reduce food wastage and strengthen its agricultural supply chain.

The ambassador also identified promising areas for joint ventures and business-to-business partnerships across agriculture, dairy, and pharmaceuticals, highlighting Argentina's advanced capabilities in oncology product manufacturing. He stated that the Argentine Embassy is fully committed to facilitating commercial connections between companies of both nations to help identify reliable partners and foster mutually beneficial trade relations. Emphasizing the economic context, Sayús noted that Argentina's exports to Pakistan reached approximately US$247 million in 2025, while Pakistan's exports to Argentina stood around US$75 million. Agriculture contributes over 5 percent to Argentina's GDP and more than 23 percent to Pakistan's GDP, with Argentina positioned globally as the third-largest food exporter.

Responding to the proposal, KCCI President Talat Mahmood emphasized the necessity of strengthening bilateral economic relations through balanced trade and the diversification of exportable products. Mahmood stressed that Pakistan must actively explore avenues to expand its exports to Argentina and narrow the widening trade imbalance. Both sides underscored the importance of private-sector engagement and exploring new commercial opportunities to grant Pakistani exporters stronger access to the Argentine market.

stories.title: Democrats Win Key Senate Races in US Midterm Elections
stories.summary:
Media projections indicate that Democrats secured major Senate victories in North Carolina and Georgia during the US midterm elections, though control of the chamber remains undecided with millions of votes uncounted. Former governor Roy Cooper easily defeated Trump-backed Republican Michael Whatley in North Carolina to capture a Republican-held seat, marking one of the four net pickups Democrats need for a majority. In Georgia, Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff defeated US Representative Mike Collins. Additionally, former Atlanta mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms won the Georgia gubernatorial race against Republican Rick Jackson, becoming the first Black woman elected governor of the state.

The elections serve as a referendum on the first two years of President Donald Trump's second term. Exit polls conducted by SSRS revealed that half of nationwide voters viewed the midterms as a chance to rebuke the president, three-quarters expressed anger or dissatisfaction with the country's direction, and 70 percent want Congress to establish more checks and balances. President Trump's approval ratings have hovered near career lows amid voter frustration over the war on Iran, higher fuel prices, and broader affordability concerns. Historically, the sitting president's party tends to lose ground in midterm elections.

To capture a Senate majority, Democrats face a narrow path requiring them to defend all existing seats while winning at least two traditionally Republican states. In the House of Representatives, where Democrats need a net gain of three seats to take control, roughly four dozen races had been called by Tuesday evening. Meanwhile, the US Justice Department deployed 1,000 election monitors across all 50 states, drawing criticism from Democrats who labeled the initiative potential voter intimidation. The Alaska Senate race also drew controversy following a New York Times report alleging that Democratic candidate Mary Peltola's campaign helped recruit an independent candidate sharing the exact name of her Republican opponent, Dan Sullivan, prompting a Justice Department criminal probe.

stories.title: International Conference Explores Future Drivers of Asian Migration
stories.summary:
Scholars and policy specialists from Pakistan, Bangladesh, India, Nepal, the Philippines, and Sri Lanka gathered in Lahore for a two-day international conference titled 'Future Drivers of International Migration from Asia.' Organized by the Centre on International Migration, Remittances and Diaspora at the Lahore School of Economics, the event focused on ensuring that migration remains humane, orderly, and sustainable. Dr. Shahid Amjad Chaudhry opened the conference by urging Pakistan to diversify its economy, expand high-value services, and prioritize education, healthcare, and IT to generate domestic employment.

CIMRAD Coordinator Dr. Nasra M. Shah shared demographic figures indicating that 83 percent of the global population resides in their country of origin, 13 percent migrate internally, and only 3.7 percent cross international borders. Keynote speaker Dr. Anna Triandafyllidou described contemporary migration as a complex, non-linear phenomenon shaped by socioeconomic and technological transformations. Academic sessions explored various regional migration trends, including Nepal's reliance on labour migration—where remittances account for 33 percent of GDP—driven by unemployment, economic uncertainty, and climate disasters. Experts also discussed how limited domestic jobs and steady overseas demand sustain migration from the Philippines.

Regarding Pakistan, Dr. G.M. Arif noted that traditional migration to Gulf Cooperation Council countries persists alongside a rise in skilled migration to Western nations. He attributed these trends to economic instability, government policies promoting overseas employment, and persistent skills mismatches. Discussant Dr. Naved Hamid emphasized that demographic pressures and limited local opportunities mean migration pressure will likely remain high in countries like Pakistan and Nepal, underscoring the need for forward-looking policies and stronger international cooperation.

stories.title: Pakistan Stock Exchange Lists Ningbo Green Light in Historic SPAC Deal
stories.summary:
Ningbo Green Light Energy Limited (NGLEL) has achieved a major milestone by becoming listed on the Main Board of the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX). This marks the completion of Pakistan’s first-ever Special Purpose Acquisition Company (SPAC) transaction. The listing was officially celebrated with a Gong Ceremony at the exchange. The business combination was successfully executed through a Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by the Lahore High Court on September 30, 2026, routing the target company LSE SPAC-I Limited into a merger with NGLEL with the structural assistance of LSE Capital.

NGLEL operates within the renewable energy sector, focusing on solar engineering, procurement, construction, system integration, and operation and maintenance services. PSX Director Ahmed Chinoy stated that the innovative transaction demonstrates alternative capital access for growth-oriented enterprises while establishing a precedent for future SPAC listings that support Pakistan's transition to renewable energy and economic ties with China. NGLEL Chief Executive Officer Muhammad Qasim emphasized that the platform enhances the company's ability to scale operations and build long-term value, supported by Director Technology Cheng Quan's vision of combining international technical expertise with local execution.

LSE Capital CEO Aftab Ahmad Chaudhry, who pioneered the SPAC framework in Pakistan, highlighted that the transaction validates the model as a credible and efficient public market entry pathway. He noted that navigating the regulatory landscape required substantial innovation and persistence.

The PSX noted that this initial SPAC listing broadens public investment opportunities and underlines the growing economic significance of the renewable energy sector in Pakistan.

stories.title: National Assembly Committee Slams Delay in Minimum Daily Wage for OPF Workers
stories.summary:
The National Assembly Standing Committee on Overseas Pakistanis has expressed strong dissatisfaction regarding the failure to enforce minimum daily wage rates for workers of the Overseas Pakistanis Foundation (OPF). Parliament approved these wage rates during the Federal Budget for 2026-27, yet four months later, the public-sector institution has still not applied them. Committee Chairman Syed Rafiullah criticized the Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis for the delay, pointing out that private entities are required to comply immediately while public workers are forced to wait.

Federal Secretary for the Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development Nadeem Aslam Chaudhry explained that institutional procedure requires a meeting and formal approval from the Ministry’s Board. He assured the committee that a resolution would be passed in an upcoming meeting within days to finalize the rates permanently. The committee recommended that all subordinate boards establish automated mechanisms to implement federal wage increases immediately upon announcement, alongside demands for stronger financial protection, better salary packages, and improved workplace safety standards for mine workers and their families.

Addressing recent safety concerns, the committee reviewed a coal mine incident in Sorrange, Balochistan, noting that three provincial mines department inspectors and two labor department officials have been suspended. Authorities have lodged First Information Reports, issued show-cause notices to responsible companies, and distributed 34 compensation cheques to affected families, while the committee urged all provinces and Gilgit-Baltistan to increase financial grants for such incidents to Rs 3 million. Additionally, the panel requested detailed financial portfolios from departments under the ministry and deferred three legislative bills—the Employees’ Old-Age Benefits, Industrial Relations, and Emigration Amendment Bills of 2026.

stories.title: Sindh Energy and Climate Conference Demands Fair Benefits for Host Communities
stories.summary:
Experts, lawmakers, and community representatives at the Sindh Energy and Climate Conference (SECC26) have demanded significant reforms in the provincial energy sector. They stressed that the transition to renewable energy must safeguard local populations, guarantee electricity access, reinforce provincial autonomy, and ensure fair economic distribution. Opening-day discussions revealed a stark contrast between high energy production and poor public access, noting that residents living near major wind and power projects continue to face power shortages, environmental degradation, and scarce job opportunities.

Research presented by Uswa Ali Memon indicated that only 16 per cent of households residing near 36 independent power producers with 1,800 megawatts of capacity are connected to the national grid. Community members reported that corporate social responsibility initiatives remain weak and voluntary, while large-scale developments like the Thar coal projects have caused land damage from wastewater, coal dust, and noise pollution without delivering promised jobs or resettlement solutions. Speakers called for mandatory CSR funds, district monitoring committees, and mandatory free, prior, and informed consent for local populations.

Furthermore, participants advocated for decentralised energy governance under Article 157 of the Constitution to expand provincial authority via the Sindh Electric Power Regulatory Authority (SEPRA). Experts also promoted microgrids and minigrids to alleviate rural electricity shortages, while calling for international climate finance to be delivered through grants rather than loans to prevent worsening debt burdens.

stories.title: Jamaat-e-Islami Inaugurates Gulshan-e-Iqbal Projects and Criticizes City Mayor
stories.summary:
Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) leaders inaugurated 25 newly constructed streets and a model neighborhood in Gulshan-e-Iqbal Town, while strongly criticizing the city mayor for urban mismanagement and incompetence. JI Karachi Chief Monem Zafar, District East chief Naeem Akhtar, and Town Chairman Dr Fawad Ahmed jointly opened the infrastructure projects, which included three primary roads inside the National Cement Society within Union Council-7.

During the ceremony, Monem Zafar claimed that while the broader city suffers from severe decay, the nine towns managed by JI function as successful development hubs. He highlighted that Gulshan Town is swiftly advancing on an ambitious initiative to build 1,005 roads and streets spanning 10 million square feet, alongside successfully restoring local parks and doubling school admissions. Zafar also criticized the ongoing University Road project under the BRT Red Line as a source of prolonged public distress due to delays.

Naeem Akhtar noted that the newly paved streets in the Cement Society are the first major infrastructure upgrades the area has received in 22 years. Dr Fawad Ahmed stated that the recently opened roads and smaller streets were completed in a rapid 11-day timeframe, urging local residents to help protect the new developments. The inauguration event drew a large gathering of local residents and municipal officials.

stories.title: Islamabad High Court Grants Protective Bail to TikToker in Sialkot Stampede Case
stories.summary:
The Islamabad High Court granted protective bail to TikToker Muhammad Ansar Jatt, also known as "Mr Patlu," in connection with a deadly stampede at his mehndi event in Sialkot. Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar issued the protective bail order, which lasts until November 10, enabling Jatt to avoid arrest and approach the appropriate court for legal remedy. Jatt arrived at the court in a wheelchair to surrender.

The incident took place on Friday night at the Faraz Cricket Ground on Daska Road, where hundreds of people had gathered for a mehndi and prize-distribution ceremony organized by Jatt. A stampede erupted when the stadium gates were opened, resulting in two deaths and 18 injuries. A first information report was subsequently registered on October 31 at the Motra Police Station against Jatt, his brother, the ground owner, six others, and between 40 and 45 unidentified security guards.

The case was registered under multiple sections of the Pakistan Penal Code, including provisions related to unintentional murder, mischief, rioting with deadly weapons, unlawful assembly, and disobedience to public servants, alongside the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance. Advocates Barrister Qasim Nawaz Abbasi and Barrister Raja Ali Abbas Jalap represented Jatt in filing the petition to prevent his arrest before reaching a competent court.

During the proceedings, defense counsel argued that while the FIR fell outside the Islamabad High Court's territorial jurisdiction, protective bail was necessary to ensure the suspect could travel safely to the court where the case was filed without being detained en route. The petition described the accusations as false and baseless, noting that Jatt had no prior criminal record. Justice Dogar acknowledged the temporary and limited nature of the protective relief, allowing the petitioner time to surrender before the proper forum.

stories.title: Government and Jamaat-e-Islami Discuss Measures to Ease Fuel Price Burdens
stories.summary:
The federal government and a delegation from Jamaat-e-Islami Pakistan held discussions in Islamabad to explore ways of mitigating the impact of petroleum prices on the general public, particularly low-income families. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar led the government side in a meeting with the JI delegation, headed by Liaquat Baloch, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Several key government officials participated in the talks, including Minister for Planning and Development Ahsan Iqbal, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Inter-Provincial Coordination and Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah Khan, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Tariq Bajwa, the finance secretary, and the special secretary. The discussions focused on identifying practical options to extend financial relief to ordinary citizens facing mounting global economic pressures.

Both sides evaluated current energy pricing models and committed to sustaining consultations over the coming days to formulate a concrete course of action. Senator Dar emphasized the administration's dedication to safeguarding public welfare and resolving the financial hardships experienced by everyday citizens.

Additionally, the Deputy Prime Minister highlighted the necessity of cross-party political engagement and dialogue when addressing national economic obstacles. Official statements confirmed that the meeting involved candid exchanges on practical relief measures, specifically targeting vulnerable low-income households, with both parties agreeing to continue working toward a shared path forward regarding energy costs.

stories.title: Hyderabad Glass Bangles Industry Faces Severe Strain Amid Gas Shortages
stories.summary:
Representatives of the Hyderabad Glass Bangle Manufacturers Association met with officials from the Hyderabad Chamber of Small Traders & Small Industry to demand urgent action against ongoing gas load-shedding and low-pressure issues. Association President Haji Saleem Khan led the delegation to the Chamber secretariat, where he stressed that resolving these fuel shortages is vital for the survival of one of Hyderabad's key industrial sectors.

According to Khan, inadequate gas supplies continue to severely disrupt factory production schedules. He added that liquefied petroleum gas, which serves as an alternative fuel source, is virtually impossible to buy at the official rate of 294 rupees per kilogram, with market prices surging to approximately 560 rupees per kilogram. He urged the Chamber leadership to advocate strongly for the industry with relevant government departments.

Chamber President Nadeem Ahmed Siddiqui responded by criticizing authorities for consistently raising tax collection targets while failing to supply industries with necessary utilities. He pointed out that the livelihoods of over 200,000 people depend on the local glass bangles trade, warning that ignoring the sector's difficulties threatens the economic stability of numerous families.

Siddiqui reiterated that gas shortages, low pressure, and exorbitant alternative fuel expenses have placed immense pressure on manufacturers. He assured the Association that the Chamber will collaborate closely with them to lobby government forums and protect both the local industry and the workers reliant upon it.

stories.title: FPCCI and ASEAN Diplomats Host Roundtable to Boost Economic and Trade Ties
stories.summary:
The Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce & Industry, alongside the Honorary Consulate General of the Philippines in Karachi, hosted the Pakistan-ASEAN Business Roundtable under the banner "Navigating Our Future Together." The gathering united ASEAN diplomats, government officials, and business leaders to foster deeper economic collaboration.

Key figures addressing the event included FPCCI Senior Vice President Saquib Fayyaz Magoon, FPCCI Committee on Diplomacy Chairman Hanif Gohar, and Ministry of Foreign Affairs Director General Irfan Soomro as the chief guest. The diplomatic contingent was spearheaded by Philippine Ambassador and ASEAN Committee in Islamabad Chair Dr Emmanuel R Fernandez, alongside ambassadors and high commissioners from Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia, Myanmar, and Brunei Darussalam, with co-hosting support from Honorary Consul General Dr Imran Yousuf.

Magoon pointed out that while ASEAN represents roughly 680 million citizens and a combined gross domestic product exceeding four trillion dollars, bilateral trade with Pakistan sits between eleven and twelve billion dollars, with Pakistani exports remaining below 1.5 billion dollars. He proposed establishing a Pakistan-ASEAN Business Forum with an FPCCI secretariat, routine trade exhibitions, business-to-business exchanges, and closer cooperation in the halal economy, alongside reviews of existing trade agreements with Indonesia and Malaysia and new preferential trade pacts.

Gohar's keynote address introduced practical proposals for regional integration, including joint ventures in corporate farming, digital services, and transport logistics. His prominent suggestion was a one-year multiple-entry "ASEAN Business Visa Sticker" for qualifying FPCCI members, alongside restored direct airline routes connecting Karachi with Kuala Lumpur, Bangkok, and Manila. Ambassador Fernandez welcomed the initiatives and promised to relay the proposals to ASEAN capitals, while other diplomats expressed enthusiasm for expanded business-to-business engagement.

Chief Guest Irfan Soomro reaffirmed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' backing for private-sector economic diplomacy regarding visas, connectivity, and trade pacts. The roundtable concluded with an agreement to draft a two-year Pakistan-ASEAN Business Cooperation Roadmap and establish quarterly meetings coordinated by the FPCCI Diplomacy Committee.

stories.title: Experts at SDPI conference highlight reforms for Pakistan's funding gap
stories.summary:
During the 29th Sustainable Development Conference organized by the Sustainable Development Policy Institute in Islamabad, experts emphasized that Pakistan requires fundamental structural reforms, mandatory corporate social responsibility legislation, and innovative financing to address its expanding social-sector funding gap. Adnan Pasha, an adviser to the finance minister, noted that international institutions like the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank expect tangible implementation rather than mere reform announcements.

Water experts at the event discussed the regional challenges of water security. Ambassador Shafqat Kakakhel, chairman of the SDPI board of governors, highlighted the Indus Waters Treaty as a crucial agreement that prevented major conflict. Meanwhile, former Federal Flood Commission chairman Ahmed Kamal pointed out that Pakistan must actively pursue its treaty rights as India advances various hydroelectric projects.

In another session, international partners praised Sindh’s post-2022 flood housing reconstruction program. SPHF Chief Executive Officer Khalid Mahmood Shaikh stated that construction has begun on roughly 1.6 million homes, with one million already completed. World Bank Country Director Bolormaa Amgaabazar and ADB Country Director Dr Emma Xiaoqin Fan commended the initiative for its beneficiary-led approach, which has also driven financial inclusion by opening about 1.7 million bank accounts.

Discussions also covered energy transition and labor rights. UNESCAP Director Mikiko Tanaka warned of hurdles regarding renewable energy integration due to seasonal variations and transmission constraints. Furthermore, Parliamentary Caucus Secretary Dr Syeda Shahida Rehmani stressed the importance of improving protections for informal workers, as climate change heavily impacts women and vulnerable groups.

stories.title: Pakistan Considers International Arbitration Against Etisalat Over Unpaid Funds
stories.summary:
The Pakistani government is evaluating the possibility of pursuing international arbitration against Etisalat to recover an outstanding payment of $800 million stemming from the 2005 sale of Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited. Alongside the principal amount, authorities are considering seeking opportunity costs accrued since 2008 and applicable damages. The development was examined during a joint session of the Senate standing committees on information technology and privatisation, where members were briefed on steps taken by the Office of the Attorney General for Pakistan.

During the proceedings, IT Secretary Zarrar Hasham Khan requested that media representatives and unauthorised individuals leave the room due to the sensitive nature of the agenda, leading to an in-camera discussion. Following the meeting, several senators voiced frustration that parliamentarians were denied access to the sale purchase agreement concerning the divestment of 26 percent shares and management control to UAE-based Etisalat International Pakistan, known today as e&. Lawmakers argued that national asset transactions should be transparently shared with parliament rather than restricted among bureaucrats.

According to documentation provided by the Ministry of Privatisation, the government originally sold the 26 percent stake and management control to Etisalat for $2.59 billion, of which $1.76 billion was successfully collected. The remaining $800 million was tied to the transfer of PTCL properties to the incoming management. Although 3,214 of the 3,246 total properties were successfully transferred, 32 properties remain untransferable, prompting Etisalat to withhold the balance.

Efforts to resolve the post-privatization impasse through various committees and negotiations since 2015 have failed to produce an agreement. Consequently, a newly formed committee recommended evaluating international arbitration pursuant to the terms of the sale purchase agreement. The attorney general has been tasked with assessing the legal merits and prospects of success before seeking final approval from the prime minister or federal cabinet to issue a notice of intent.

stories.title: State Bank Governor Emphasizes Protecting Vulnerable Groups from Climate Shocks
stories.summary:
